thread:
maria: quick sync — i'm proposing we stop making each language SDK own exporter buffering/fanout and instead ship a small 'exporter-proxy' sidecar that handles per-tenant routing, retention, backpressure and retries. gist: https://gist.redwood/example-exporter-proxy (very rough).

ajay: curious — main win is centralizing retry/tenant-multiplex, right? what about latency overhead?

maria: yep, centralizes the hard bits (fanout, retention TTLs, multitenant headers). we keep SDKs tiny (emit OTLP to localhost) so language lifecycle differences are isolated. overhead should be minimal on local IPC/gRPC.

liam: +1 for surface area reduction. big practical win: python gunicorn pre-fork issues. if apps rely on exporters that open sockets at import-time we see double-connections. we already have bugs from that. sidecar avoids per-worker exporter lifecycle traps.

ajay: exactly — in Go we tend to init a global exporter once and rely on graceful shutdown via contexts. but in python we need an explicit post-fork init or use preexec_fn. this is brittle. sidecar seems cleaner.

sasha: operational concerns: sidecar becomes another piece to manage. how do we configure per-tenant retention? dynamic config API?

maria: idea: sidecar exposes a gRPC /config stream from control-plane; sidecar applies tenant routing policies and retention TTLs locally. SDKs just add tenant id as resource attr.

jenna: otel-bot: current ingest limits: 2000 spans/s per ingestion shard; retention tiers: 7d/30d/90d. see /policies.

liam: what about sampling? do we sample at SDK or proxy? sampling at SDK saves network/cpu, but we lose ability to do deterministic or downstream sampling by business rules.

maria: hybrid: SDK does cheap head-sampling (fractional by service) to avoid extreme noise; sidecar can apply policy sampling (by tenant/route/debug flags) and decide to keep/upgrade certain traces for evals.

ajay: shutdown semantics we need to nail: python atexit doesn't always run (SIGKILL, container OOM); gunicorn workers fork; go uses signal.Notify with context cancel; rust tasks drop on panic. exporter-proxy lets us rely on proxy to drain on lifecycle and gives SDKs a simpler best-effort flush.

liam: +1. also saves per-language exporter implementations — fewer bugs around batching semantics. we can centralize batching configuration (max_batch_size, linger_ms).

maria: draft SDK init examples i sketched for each language:

```python
# python (fastapi/uvicorn or gunicorn):
from redwood_otel import init_agent
init_agent(local_endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:4318", resource_attrs={"service.name": "embedder", "tenant.id": os.getenv("TENANT_ID")})
# keep minimal: no exporter wiring in app code
```

```go
// go (long-lived server)
func main() {
  otelcfg.InitAgent("localhost:4317", map[string]string{"service.name":"router"})
  ctx := context.Background()
  // regular shutdown pattern cancels ctx, agent/sidecar can drain
}
```

```rust
// rust (tokio)
let _agent = telemetry::agent::start("127.0.0.1:4318", resource_map!("service.name" => "model"));
// keep handle alive in runtime; don't block on flush in drop, sidecar handles durable delivery
```

sasha: nice. one more: what about local disk buffering when sidecar temporarily down? we should avoid unbounded queues. bounded disk buffer with eviction/oldest-first + metrics.

maria: yes bounded file-queue on sidecar only, SDK keeps memory queue small. we'll expose metrics: queued_spans, dropped_spans, last_flush_ms to console.

ajay: telemetry UX: for devs we should offer a single line env var to opt into sidecar vs direct export. e.g., REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE=proxy|direct. default proxy for hosted/dedicated.

liam: testing matrix: python (gunicorn/uvicorn), go (net/http + graceful), rust (tokio multi-thread). i'll add repros for pre-fork and signal interactions.

jenna: otel-bot: created ticket INF-5423 to track exporter-proxy work + test matrix.

maria: next steps: i'll write a short RFC with tradeoffs and perf numbers (IPC p95 overhead) and a minimal PoC sidecar. volunteers for language init stubs?

ajay: i'll take python stubs + a pre-fork test.

liam: i'll do go + perf harness.

sasha: i'll prototype sidecar buffer + config gRPC.

maria: thanks — i'll draft RFC today and @jenna please add infra cost model to INF-5423. :thumbsup:

otel-bot: reaction: :white_check_mark: RFC created -> INF-5423/epic
